Tip: import from Syride first, then add your tracks. Each track is attached to its Syride flight.

Syride knows more about a flight than its track: the site, the distance and the wing. Tracks imported afterwards are attached to these flights, found by the Syride id in a downloaded file's name or by the take-off time, so each flight is in the logbook once. Tracks imported first become flights of their own, and a later Syride import would add the same flights again.

Each track is compared with the flights in your logbook:
A file named after a Syride flight number, as downloaded from the Syride website, belongs to that flight.
A track that starts in the minute of a flight's take-off time belongs to that flight. This is how the files of a Syride logger are found.
A flight on the same day with a similar duration is only a possible match. Choose “Attach” if it is the right one.
Times are compared in your computer's time zone, so flights made in another time zone only show as possible matches. A flight that already has a track keeps it.
The first row with a value is taken as the header, and the columns are matched by it. Change any that are wrong.
